learning_objective: 🎯 Trace the major shifts from the 1990s onward: the rise of coalition politics, the Mandal Commission, economic liberalization, and the politics of religion!

main_concepts.concept_title: 📉 The End of the Congress System
main_concepts.simple_explanation: The 1989 elections marked the end of the dominant one-party era. No single party secured a clear majority, officially launching the long era of multi-party Coalition Governments at the center.

In 1990, the National Front government decided to implement the Mandal Commission recommendation: granting 27% reservation in central government jobs for Other Backward Classes (OBCs), sparking intense nationwide protests.

Facing a severe financial crisis, India initiated massive economic reforms (Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation), completely changing the socialist direction the country had followed since independence.

The demolition of the disputed Babri Masjid structure in 1992 escalated communal tensions. Simultaneously, the BJP experienced a massive political rise by mobilizing support around 'Hindutva' and the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.

Despite intense political rivalries, most major parties eventually agreed on four main things: the new economic policies, acceptance of OBC reservations, the role of state-level parties in central government, and a focus on pragmatic politics over rigid ideology.

fun_activity.title: 🔗 The Coalition Jigsaw
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you lead a political party that won 200 seats, but you need 272 to form a government. You have to convince 3 smaller regional parties to join you. Write down one cabinet minister position you would offer each to build your 'Coalition'!

exam_tips: 📌 The period post-1989 is defined by 'Coalition Politics'—where regional parties became kingmakers at the national level.
📌 Clearly explain what 'Mandal' refers to in Indian politics: the political mobilization and reservation policies for Other Backward Classes (OBCs).
📌 Always mention the structural shift in 1991: India moved away from a state-controlled 'Mixed Economy' toward a market-driven 'Liberalised' economy.
quick_recap: ⭐ The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and United Progressive Alliance (UPA) became the two major coalition alliances in Indian politics.
⭐ The assassination of Rajiv Gandhi in 1991 significantly altered the leadership dynamics of the Congress party.
⭐ Despite intense polarization on religious and caste lines in the 90s, Indian democracy showed resilience by forming a broad consensus on development and governance.
